# <span id="aanchor219"></span> Gas Loss Tickets

The Gas Loss Ticket Viewer is used for viewing and creating Gas Loss ticket data. Gas loss tickets are used to account for unmeasured gas volumes such as from the blowdown of a line. You can view and edit Gas Loss tickets in the Gas Loss Ticket Editor as well as Ticket Search.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Gas Loss Ticket Viewer and view Gas Loss tickets:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Tickets** \> **Gas Loss Tickets**.
2.  Specify a date range and click **Refresh**. All saved Gas Loss tickets will display.
3.  Double-click a ticket entry to view the ticket details.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 537;height: 362;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Add Ticket">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Add a Gas Loss Ticket</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Add Ticket">

<div class="procedure">

To create a Gas Loss ticket:

1.  Refresh the Gas Loss Ticket Viewer.

2.  Right-click anywhere on the grid and select **New Ticket**.

3.  Enter the date and time for the ticket. This will dictate when it is included in balances as well as what month it is in for month end closing..

4.  Select a ticket type from the **Type** drop-down menu.

5.  Depending on the type that you select, you must select a mainline, a mainline and a lateral, or a mainline and a compressor. These must be created in the Pipeline Editor before the Gas Loss ticket is created.

6.  Select a meter class (required if the [Subtotal by Meter Class option](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#SubtotalClass) is enabled). A default value for this data point be configured on the [FLOWCAL Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md) screen.

    All gas loss tickets are assigned with a direction as specified in [FLOWCAL Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#GasLossTicket).

7.  Select a calculation method. Available options are:

    - **Manual** – This is the default calculation method. When this option is selected, you must enter an actual volume. The volume must be at base conditions as no calculations are done on the volume.
    - **Blowdown** – When this option is selected, the actual volume will be populated from the selected mainline, lateral, or compressor, depending on the ticket type. You will then need to enter the pressure and temperature of the gas at the start and end of the blowdown, whether the pressure measurement is gauge or absolute, and the atmospheric pressure for gauge measurements. From this, FLOWCAL will calculate the amount of gas loss at base conditions.
    - **Pinched Valve** – When this option is selected, you must specify the valve information, starting and ending pressure, elapsed time for the valve to be open, whether the pressure measurement is gauge or absolute, and the atmospheric pressure for gauge measurements. From this, FLOWCAL will calculate the amount of gas loss at base conditions.

    If a gas quality source for the Gas Loss ticket is selected at the bottom of the Gas Loss Ticket Editor, and it has a sample that encompasses the Gas Loss ticket, it will be used to calculate the energy; otherwise, you must manually enter an energy value or leave the Energy field blank. Analysis information can be viewed on the Analyses tab.

    Once the ticket is saved, the calculation method cannot be changed.

8.  Location will be set based on the setup of the selected mainline, lateral, or compressor. This dictates what balance the gas loss ticket will go into, if any. Users may override this.

9.  Select an edit reason from the drop-down menu and click **Save**.

10. Click **Edit** to make revisions to the data at any time.

The location rollup process totals the appropriate values associated with gas loss tickets. The source analysis apply routine implements a gas quality source for a gas loss ticket upon saving the gas loss ticket. If the calculation method is "Blowdown", the calculated volume is based on the compressibility values determined using the applied gas quality Z method. Calculated energy is based on the applied gas quality dry heating value.

</div>

</div>

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Add a Ticket Note</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ticket Note">

If a ticket includes a note, note icon next to the ticket will be yellow. The icon will be gray if no note is attached. Right-click the note icon to access options for viewing or adding notes.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Close Ticket">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Close a Ticket</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Close Ticket">

<div class="procedure">

To close a Gas Loss ticket in the Gas Loss Ticket Editor:

1.  Refresh the Gas Loss Ticket Viewer.
2.  Select one or more Gas Loss tickets. Exceptions on each ticket must have been acknowledged or resolved before the ticket can be closed.
3.  Right click on the grid and select **Close Ticket**.

Once a ticket has been closed, the closed values display on the Close Data tab.

</div>

</div>
